question: Whether removal of the application memory.current >= memory.max stop can be defensible while the existing kernel cap and all other guards remain unchanged.
decision: Defensible as a separately frozen bounded loader experiment if the residual shared-cgroup risk is accepted; not equivalent to the old policy, a safety proof, or evidence that the model fits. Root deferred any experiment until source preparation and checkpoint persistence.
observed_result: The v17.1 application watchdog killed partial loading at sampled shared cgroup total equal to 8 GiB; owned-group RSS and pressure proxy were below their stops and observed OOM/OOM-kill counter deltas were zero. No health, tokenization or generation success was obtained.

primary_source.interpretation: The hard-limit path tries reclaim and reaches OOM if usage cannot be reduced. Equality, temporary overrun, and a max event are not themselves proof of OOM. The documentation allows some allocation failures without OOM events. Cgroup OOM containment does not isolate peers inside that cgroup.

proxy_uncertainty: The nine-component sum deliberately excludes ordinary unmapped clean file cache and overlaps some categories. It is not a certified upper bound on unreclaimable working memory.
Counters are read nonatomically. Partial-loading RSS is not the completed reader working set.
File-cache contribution to the equality stop is plausible but unproven; no reclaimability attribution or fit guarantee follows.
concrete_risks: Reclaim failure can kill a peer in the shared cgroup before a sampled watcher observes an OOM increment.
The gap between the 7 GiB proxy stop and 8 GiB kernel hard limit is heuristic headroom; fast allocations and uncoordinated peers can consume it.
Reclaim can stall or thrash; existing startup and wall limits bound duration but do not certify progress.
necessary_unchanged_conditions: Exact 8 GiB kernel memory.max, with no cgroup setting mutation.
Prelaunch 4.25 GiB owned-process-group reserve plus proxy strictly below 7 GiB.
4.25 GiB owned-process-group RSS, 7 GiB proxy, 5.5 GiB address-space, startup/wall/CPU caps.
OOM increment/reset, missing telemetry, anchored ownership, independent kill and final cleanup checks.
One separately frozen zero-generation attempt in an exclusive heavy window after artifact checkpointing; preserve both earlier failures and actual total/max/event telemetry.
Independent review of the concrete guard-only code diff before any execution.
root_checkpoint_decision: Finish source preparation and persist v17 first; the policy remains a proposal in this checkpoint.
